Key corrections: Redshift has no native cross-region automated snapshots (unlike RDS)-use manual snapshots copied via AWS Backup or S3 cross-region replication for standby data. Redshift 'hot standby' is a misnomer-you restore from snapshot (minutes to hours depending on data size); true hot standby requires RA3 with cross-region read replicas. The architecture separates detection (CloudWatch/Glue DQ), orchestration (Step Functions), and execution (Lambda with cross-account STS AssumeRole). Critical components include: cross-region S3 CRR with bucket policies for data redundancy, Glue Catalog partitioning for validation queries using Athena, and Route53 weighted routing for traffic cutover. Rollback procedure: revert Route53 weighted routing to original weights, delete promoted Redshift cluster to stop billing, re-enable S3 bucket policies for write access, and clear DynamoDB global table replica flags. Estimated RTO: 15-30 minutes for detection, 5-10 minutes for isolation, 10-60 minutes for Redshift restore, 5-10 minutes for validation, totaling 35-105 minutes depending on data volume.
